Severe Flooding Hits Retail Sites Across Northern Spain

Floodwaters have caused significant disruption to retail industry sites across northern Spain, as heavy rainfall continues to lash the region for a fifth consecutive day. Major retail chains, including Almacenes del Norte and SuperCentro Ibérico, have reported extensive damage to dozens of their stores and distribution hubs in areas such as Santander, Bilbao and Gijón.

According to industry sources, more than 60 retail locations have been forced to suspend operations due to inundated premises and unsafe conditions for workers. Speaking from an affected site in Bilbao, María Sánchez, a regional manager for Almacenes del Norte, said, “We have never seen flooding reach this level. Our priority is ensuring the safety of our employees, some of whom have been unable to leave the premises due to rising water.”

The Spanish Retail Federation estimates that over 1,500 workers have been impacted, with some stores reporting water levels reaching up to half a meter inside sales areas and stockrooms. “We are coordinating with site managers to provide support to staff and assess the extent of the damage. Many colleagues are facing difficult conditions,” said Federico Ruiz, spokesperson for the Retail Workers’ Union.

Industry analysts warn that the longer the flooding persists, the greater the risk of structural damage to retail facilities and losses from water-ruined inventory. Some sites have activated emergency protocols, moving stock to higher shelves and placing sandbags at entrances, but with rainfall forecast to continue, the situation remains critical for retail operators and their staff.
